In general, first editions of a works in English were prioritized, although there are a number of works in other languages, notably Latin and Welsh, included and sometimes a second or later edition of a work was chosen if there was a compelling reason to do so.

div.head: GOD Glorified in Man's Dependance.

q.p: That no Fleſhflesh ſhouldshould Gloryglory in his Preſencepresence. But of him are ye in ChriſtChrist JeſusJesus, who of God is made unto us Wiſdomwisdom, and Righteouſneſsrighteousness, and Sanctificationsanctification, and Redemptionredemption: Thatthat according as it is written, Hehe that glorieth let him glory in the Lord.

div.p: THOSEThose ChriſtiansChristians to whom the Apoſtleapostle directed this Epiſtleepistle, dwelt in a Partpart of the Worldworld where human Wiſdomwisdom was in great Reputerepute; as the Apoſtleapostle obſervesobserves in the 22. VerſeVerse22nd verse of this Chapterchapter, The Greeks ſeekseek after Wiſdomwisdom. Corinth was not far from Athens, that had been for many Agesages the moſtmost famous Seatseat of Philoſophyphilosophy and Learninglearning in the Worldworld.

The Apoſtleapostle therefore obſervesobserves to them how that God by the Goſpelgospel deſtroyeddestroyed, and brought to nought, their human Wiſdomwisdom. The Learnedlearned Grecians, and their great Philoſophersphilosophers, by all their Wiſdomwisdom did not know God, they were not able to find out the Truthtruth in divine Thingsthings. But after they had done their utmoſtutmost to no Effecteffect, it
pleaſedpleased God at length, to reveal himſelfhimself by the Goſpelgospel which they accounted Fooliſhneſsfoolishness: Hehe choſechose the fooliſhfoolish things of the Worldworld, to confound the wiſewise, and the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty, and the baſebase things of the world, and things that are deſpiſeddespised, yea and things which are not; to bring to nought the things that are. And the Apoſtleapostle informs them why he thus did, in the Verſeverse of the Texttext, That no Fleſhflesh ſhouldshould glory in his Preſencepresence &cetc. —
In which Wordswords may be obſervedobserved,

1. What God aims at in the Diſpoſitiondisposition of things in the Affairaffair of Redemptionredemption, viz. thatThat Manman ſhouldshould not glory in himſelfhimself, but alone in God; That no Fleſhflesh ſhouldshould glory in his Preſencepresence, — that according as it is written he that glories let him glory in the Lord.

2. How this Endend is attained in the Workwork of Redemptionredemption, viz. byBy that abſoluteabsolute and immediate Dependancedependencedependance which Menmen have upon God in that Workwork, for all their Goodgood. InaſmuchInasmuch as,

FirſtFirst, Allall the Goodgood that they have is in and through ChriſtChrist; Hehe is made unto us Wiſdomwisdom, Righteouſneſsrighteousness, Sanctificationsanctification, and Redemptionredemption. All the Goodgood of the fallen and redeemed Creaturecreature is concerned in theſethese four things, and can't be better diſtributeddistributed than into them; but ChriſtChrist is each of them to us, and we have none of them any otherwiſeotherwise than in him. He is made of God unto us Wiſdomwisdom: Inin him are all the proper Goodgood, and true Excellencyexcellency of the Underſtandingunderstanding. WiſdomWisdom was a thing that the Greeks admired; but ChriſtChrist is the true Lightlight of the Worldworld, 'tis through him alone that true Wiſdomwisdom is imparted to the Mindmind. 'Tis in and by ChriſtChrist that we have Righteouſneſsrighteousness: 'Tis'tis by being in him that we are juſtifiedjustified, have our
Sinssins pardoned, and are received as righteous into God's Favourfavorfavour. 'Tis by ChriſtChrist that we have Sanctificationsanctification: Wewe have in him true Excellencyexcellency of Heartheart, as well as of Underſtandingunderstanding; and Hehe is made unto us inherent as well as imputed Righteouſneſsrighteousness. 'Tis by ChriſtChrist that we have Redemptionredemption, or the actual Deliverancedeliverance from all Miſerymisery, and the Beſtowmentbestowment of all Happineſshappiness and Gloryglory. Thus we have all our Goodgood by ChriſtChrist who is God.

Secondly, Anotheranother Inſtanceinstance wherein our Dependancedependencedependance on God for all our Goodgood appears, is this, Thatthat 'tis God that has given us ChriſtChrist, that we might have theſethese Benefitsbenefits through him; he of God is made unto us Wiſdomwisdom, Righteouſneſsrighteousness &cetc.

Thirdly, 'Tis'tis of him that we are in ChriſtChrist JeſusJesus, and come to have an Intereſtinterest in him, and ſoso do receive thoſethose Bleſſingsblessings which he is made unto us. 'Tis God that gives us Faithfaith whereby we cloſeclose with ChriſtChrist.

So that in this Verſeverse is ſhewnshown our Dependancedependencedependance on each Perſonperson in the Trinity for all our Goodgood. We are dependent on ChriſtChrist the Son of God, as he is our WiſdomWisdom, Righteouſneſsrighteousness, Sanctificationsanctification, and Redemptionredemption. We are dependent on the Father, who has given us ChriſtChrist, &and made him to be theſethese things to us. We are dependent on the HolyHolyholy GhoſtGhost, for 'tis of him that we are in ChriſtChrist JeſusJesus; 'tis the Spirit of God that gives Faithfaith in him, whereby we receive him, and cloſeclose with him.

DOCTDoct. GODGod is glorified in the Workwork of Redemptionredemption in this, that there appears in it ſoso abſoluteabsolute and univerſaluniversal a Dependancedependencedependance of the Redeemedredeemed on him.

Here I propoſepropose to ſhewshow, 1. That there is an abſoluteabsolute &and univerſaluniversal Dependancedependencedependance of the Redeemedredeemed on God for all their Goodgood. And 2. That God hereby is exalted and glorified in the Workwork of Redemptionredemption.

I. There is an abſoluteabsolute and univerſaluniversal Dependancedependencedependance of the Redeemedredeemed on God. The Naturenature and Contrivancecontrivance of our Redemptionredemption is ſuchsuch, that the Redeemedredeemed are in every thing directly, immediately, and intirelyentirely dependent on God: Theythey are dependent on him for all, and are dependent on him every Wayway.

The ſeveralseveral Waysways wherein the Dependancedependencedependance of one Beingbeing may be upon another for its Goodgood, and wherein the Redeemedredeemed of JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist depend on God for all their Goodgood, are theſethese, viz. That they have all their Goodgood of him, and that they have all through him, and that they have all in him: Thatthat he be the Cauſecause and Originaloriginal whence all their Goodgood comes, therein it is of him; and that he be the Mediummedium by which it is obtained and conveyed, therein they have it through him; and that he be that Goodgood it ſelfselfitself that is given and conveyed, therein it is in him.
Now thoſethose that are redeemed by JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist do in all theſethese Reſpectsrespects very directly and entirely depend on God for their all.

FirſtFirst, Thethe Redeemedredeemed have all their Goodgood of God. God is the great Authorauthor of it; Hehe is the firſtfirst Cauſecause of it, and not only ſoso but he is the only proper Cauſecause.

'Tis of God that we have our Redeemer. 'Tis God that has provided a SaviourSavior for us. JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist is not only of God in his Perſonperson, as he is
the only begotten Son of God; but he is from God as we are concerned in him, and in his Officeoffice of Mediator; Hehe is the Giftgift of God to us: God choſechose and anointed him, appointed him his Workwork, and ſentsent him into the Worldworld.

Eph. 2.:8. For by Gracegrace ye are ſavedsaved, through Faithfaith; and that not of your ſelvesselvesyourselves, it is the Giftgift of God. The Redeemedredeemed have all,

1. Of the Gracegrace of God. It was of meermere Gracegrace that God gave us his only begotten Son. The Gracegrace is great in proportion to the Dignitydignity and Excellencyexcellency of what is given: Thethe Giftgift was infinitely precious, becauſebecause it was of a Perſonperson infinitely worthy, a Perſonperson of infinite Gloryglory: and alſoalso becauſebecause it was of a Perſonperson infinitely near and dear to God.
